Compute Match — Platform Admin Guide
Platform Admins are NVIDIA staff (roles such as platform_business_admin ,
platform_business_admin_super_user , platform_business_admin_ops_user ) who run the marketplace.
They use the same /provider/*  pages as NCPs, with extra pages and cross-NCP visibility. The
header shows the persona label Platform Admin.

Global Capacity Explorer
A read-only world view of all GPU capacity across NCPs.
Filters: Search, Platform (required for the chart), Geographical Region, NCP, Country / Data
Centre Location, Start Date, End Date.
Map | List toggle. The map shows capacity hotspots; “No datacenter locations match the
current ﬁlters.” when empty.
Available Capacity chart over time, colour-coded per NCP (same colour for current and
future). Tooltips show the month’s peak-day total, current and future split, and per-city
breakdown.
Export to Excel and Export to CSV.
API: GET /api/v1/provider/global-capacity-map .
Review Future Capacities
NCP uploads that include rows starting more than 90 days out wait here.
Tabs: All, Pending, Accepted, Rejected. Filter by NCP.
Columns: NCP, File Name (click for details), Uploaded Date, Status, Actions.
Accept: conﬁrm in Approve Future Capacity Submission; status becomes Accepted and
capacity goes live for customers.
Reject: enter a reason (required, up to 500 characters) and click Submit Rejection; the NCP
is emailed the reason.
Nothing is accepted or rejected automatically; submissions wait until reviewed.
Onboard NCPs
1. Download the NCP onboarding CSV template.
2. Fill in the NCP organizations and users.
3. Upload. A background Temporal ProviderOnboardingWorkflow  validates the ﬁle, creates
Keycloak organizations, users, roles and the offering-validator  group membership, and
sends welcome emails.
4. Watch status in the history table. Onboarding job statuses: QUEUED, VALIDATING,
VALIDATION_FAILED, ONBOARDING, COMPLETED, FAILED.
Review Onboarding Requests (access requests)
When the NPN portal integration is on, partner users whose NCP is not onboarded appear here.
Approve provisions them like a CSV onboarding; Reject requires a reason and emails it. API:
/api/v1/provider/access-requests  (+ /approve , /reject ).
Custom requests
Route: /provider/custom-requests . Table only (no split view, no NCP ﬁlter). Filter by Platform,
Country, Geographical Region, Status, Sort.
Lifecycle you control: - Open →  In Review (you are working on it) - In Review or Open →  Matched
(Mark as Matched / Conﬁrm Match, optionally record the NCP, NCP region and a comment) - →
Unserviceable (Close as Unserviceable) - Customers alone can Cancel while Open or In Review.
- Matched, Unserviceable and Cancelled are ﬁnal; a request never returns to Open. The customer is
emailed on each change.

revive an Expired offering back to its prior active status.
User operations
Operations users ( operations  role) can activate pending users, list users, resend activation magic
links and delete users through the Operations APIs ( /api/v1/...  under the Operations tag).
Daily alert email
Every day at 09:00 UTC a Temporal schedule ( in-process-requests-alert-daily ) emails Platform
Admins a digest of In Process offerings approaching their contract deadline.
Analytics
The external Dashboard link opens Superset. See the analytics document for the dashboards
(Marketplace metrics and Feedback).
